tasks.prompt: Every video-to-video render started from the Video studio's source clip fails after it is queued. These models publish `durations: ["Auto"]` in the catalog; the operator's pre-flight accepts only that value, so the request body built in `src/lib/studio/video-request.ts` sends `duration: "Auto"`, and the provider then refuses the job at retrieve with `duration must be a positive number (input video duration in seconds)`. A number is refused by the pre-flight. Make the request body of a video-to-video model work: the source clip must set the length. Leave the upscalers' contract as it is.

Canvas runs of a Studio workflow ignore the step cache: running the same workflow twice regenerates every step, and the level-by-level scheduling, failure isolation and rate-limit wait budget the caller asked for do not apply either. The unit tests of the cache and the scheduler call `runWorkflow` directly and pass; the canvas goes through `runAndSaveWorkflow` in `src/lib/studio/workflow-run.ts`. Make canvas runs honour every run option the caller passes.

tasks.prompt: On a slow machine, opening a workflow in the Studio editor can save it with no steps: the next time it is opened the canvas is empty ("The workflow is empty."). The editor's first render has the workflow from the library but an empty canvas; the steps arrive with the first hydrate, one render later, and the debounced save can fire in between. Fix `src/components/studio/WorkflowStudio.tsx` so that the graph the save, the validation and the run picture read never pairs a workflow with a canvas that has not been hydrated from it yet.

When a Studio workflow contains a list (for example a two-line text list feeding a voice step), the run works but the canvas shows no result on the list's steps: the copies made for each item (`voice#0`, `voice#1`) belong to no visible step. The view is built in `src/components/studio/workflow/useRunPicture.ts`. Make each step show the results of its list items.

The sidebar footer still reads "Sign in" after the person signs in while the app is open: `SidebarIdentity` reads the account status once, at mount. Make the account status observable: in `src/lib/account.ts`, every account command that answers with an `AccountStatus` publishes it to subscribers (a `watchAccountStatus(listener)` function returning an unsubscribe function), a failed command publishes nothing, and the sidebar footer subscribes. Keep the exact call shape no-argument commands have today when they reach the bridge.

Account synchronisation failures all show "Synchronization could not finish. Try again." because most of the error codes the native side emits have no sentence. Move the mapping out of `AccountSettingsSection.tsx` into a new module `src/lib/account-sync-error.ts` exporting `accountSyncErrorMessage(code)` and the list of known codes, give every `sync_*` code the Rust sources under `src-tauri/src/account/` can emit its own sentence (through `t()`, with the French translation in the catalogs), never advise trying again for codes that mean work is in flight or waiting (`sync_local_work_active`, `sync_pending_changes`, `sync_dependencies_pending`), and never leak a path, host or native detail in a message.

diff --git a/src/lib/account-sync-error.ts b/src/lib/account-sync-error.ts
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..d3e324c71
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/lib/account-sync-error.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+import { t } from "./i18n";
+
+/**
+ * What a failed synchronisation says to the person who owns the data.
+ *
+ * Never the native or server detail, and never a filename: the point is what
+ * to do next. Several of these are not failures at all — work in flight, a
+ * change waiting on another — and say so, because "try again" is wrong advice
+ * for something that finishes on its own.
+ */
+export function accountSyncError(code: string): string {
+  switch (code) {
+    case "sync_file_too_large":
+      return t(
+        "A file exceeds the sync size limit and remains on this device. Use a smaller copy to sync it.",
+      );
+    case "sync_object_too_large":
+      return t(
+        "Some content exceeds the sync size limit and remains on this device. Reduce its size to sync it.",
+      );
+    case "account_network":
+    case "sync_timeout":
+    case "sync_blob_request_failed":
+      return t(
+        "The sync service is unavailable or did not respond in time. Your changes will retry automatically.",
+      );
+    case "account_not_connected":
+    case "sync_authentication_failed":
+      return t("Sign in again to resume synchronization.");
+    case "vault_locked":
+      return t("Open your vault to resume synchronization.");
+    case "sync_file_unavailable":
+      return t(
+        "A file could not be read on this device. Check that it is available, then try again.",
+      );
+    case "sync_file_changed":
+      return t("A file changed while it was being sent. It will be sent again on its own.");
+    case "sync_file_type_unsupported":
+      return t("This kind of file is not synchronized. It stays on this device.");
+    case "sync_local_work_active":
+    case "sync_pending_changes":
+    case "sync_dependencies_pending":
+      return t("Synchronization is waiting for work on this device to finish. Nothing is lost.");
+    case "sync_conflict_requires_review":
+      return t("Two devices changed the same thing. Review the conflict to choose what to keep.");
+    case "sync_resolution_invalid":
+      return t("That choice no longer applies. Reload the conflict and choose again.");
+    case "sync_blob_invalid":
+    case "sync_format_invalid":
+      return t(
+        "Some content did not match what this version understands, and was left alone. Update your apps, then try again.",
+      );
+    default:
+      return t("Synchronization could not finish. Your local copies are preserved. Try again.");
+  }
+}

tasks.prompt: In onboarding, the dictation practice step refuses short replies: dictating "Yes" or "OK" does not count as a success. Any non-blank reply should complete the step (`src/components/onboarding/steps/PracticeStep.tsx`).

When a person types notes above the generated summary of a meeting note (rather than below it), those notes are lost the next time the note is regenerated: `manual_notes_for_generation` in `src-tauri/src/domain/processing.rs` only keeps what follows the generated text. Keep the manual notes wherever they are: text after the generated summary first, otherwise text before it.

A note recorded in several recording sessions shows its source transcripts out of order: `source_transcripts` in `src-tauri/src/db/repositories.rs` orders by `turn_index` first, so turn 0 of the second session comes before turn 5 of the first. Order the transcripts by recording session (when it started, then insertion order), then by turn, start time and creation, with a stable last tie-breaker.

+        .await

+        .await
+        .expect("task should cancel");
+
+    let started = repos
+        .update_agent_task_status_if_in(
+            &task.id,
+            AgentTaskStatus::Running,
+            Some("Preparing"),
+            None,
+            &[AgentTaskStatus::Queued],
+        )
+        .await
+        .expect("guarded update should succeed");
+    assert!(!started);
+    let paused = repos
+        .update_agent_task_status_if_in(
+            &task.id,
+            AgentTaskStatus::Paused,
+            Some("Paused"),
+            None,
+            &[AgentTaskStatus::Running],
+        )
+        .await
+        .expect("guarded update should succeed");
+    assert!(!paused);
+
+    let loaded = repos
+        .get_agent_task(&task.id)
+        .await
+        .expect("task should load");
+    assert_eq!(loaded.status, AgentTaskStatus::Cancelled);

+#[tokio::test]
+async fn hydrated_messages_dedupe_by_external_id_and_legacy_content() {
+    let repos = test_repositories().await;
+    let task = repos
+        .create_agent_task(
+            "Find the meeting notes",
+            None,
+            AgentSafetyProfile::default(),
+        )
+        .await
+        .expect("task should be created");
+
+    let inserted = repos
+        .add_agent_message_if_absent(
+            &task.id,
+            AgentMessageRole::Assistant,
+            "Found three matching notes.",
+            "2026-06-09T10:00:00.000Z",
+            "hermes:session-1:42",
+        )
+        .await
+        .expect("first insert should succeed");
+    assert!(inserted);
+
+    // Same Hermes message hydrated again (e.g. by a concurrent poll).
+    let duplicate = repos
+        .add_agent_message_if_absent(
+            &task.id,
+            AgentMessageRole::Assistant,
+            "Found three matching notes.",
+            "2026-06-09T10:00:00.000Z",
+            "hermes:session-1:42",
+        )
+        .await
+        .expect("second insert should succeed");
+    assert!(!duplicate);
+
+    // A different Hermes message with identical content is a new message.
+    let distinct = repos
+        .add_agent_message_if_absent(
+            &task.id,
+            AgentMessageRole::Assistant,
+            "Found three matching notes.",
+            "2026-06-09T10:05:00.000Z",
+            "hermes:session-1:43",
+        )
+        .await
+        .expect("third insert should succeed");
+    assert!(distinct);
+
+    // Rows hydrated before external ids existed are matched by content.
+    repos
+        .add_agent_message(&task.id, AgentMessageRole::Assistant, "Legacy reply.")
+        .await
+        .expect("legacy message should be added");
+    let legacy_duplicate = repos
+        .add_agent_message_if_absent(
+            &task.id,
+            AgentMessageRole::Assistant,
+            "Legacy reply.",
+            "2026-06-09T10:10:00.000Z",
+            "hermes:session-1:44",
+        )
+        .await
+        .expect("legacy-matching insert should succeed");
+    assert!(!legacy_duplicate);
+
+    let loaded = repos
+        .get_agent_task(&task.id)
+        .await
+        .expect("task should load");
+    let assistant_messages = loaded
+        .messages
+        .iter()
+        .filter(|message| message.role == AgentMessageRole::Assistant)
+        .count();
+    assert_eq!(assistant_messages, 3);
+}
